field.label: Identifier
field.help: Technical identifier of the interface, used by hasync for example.

field.label: Enabled
field.help: Enable this interface.

field.label: Lock
field.help: Prevent interface removal.

field.label: Description
field.help: You may enter a description here for your reference (not parsed).

field.label: Device
field.help: Device name to connect this interface to.

field.label: Promiscuous mode
field.help: Put interface into permanently promiscuous mode. Only to be used for specific usecases requiring the interface to receive all packets being received. When unsure, leave this disabled.

field.label: MAC address (spoof)
field.help: This field can be used to spoof the MAC address of the interface. Enter a MAC address in the following format: xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx or leave blank if unsure. This may only be required e.g. with certain cable connections on a WAN interface. When used on a single VLAN interface the setting "Promiscuous mode" is required for this to work. Alternatively, the parent interface MAC can be spoofed applying the MAC address to all attached VLAN children automatically.

field.label: MTU
field.help: If you leave this field blank, the adapter's default MTU will be used. This is typically 1500 bytes but can vary in some circumstances.

field.label: MSS
field.help: If you enter a value in this field, then MSS clamping for TCP connections to the value entered above minus 40 (IPv4) or 60 (IPv6) will be in effect (TCP/IP header size).

field.label: Overwrite global settings
field.help: Overwrite custom interface hardware settings with settings specified below

field.label: Hardware CRC
field.help: Checking this option will disable hardware checksum offloading. Checksum offloading is broken in some hardware, particularly some Realtek cards. Rarely, drivers may have problems with checksum offloading and some specific NICs.

field.label: Hardware TSO
field.help: Checking this option will disable hardware TCP segmentation offloading (TSO, TSO4, TSO6). This offloading is broken in some hardware drivers, and may impact performance with some specific NICs.

field.label: Hardware LRO
field.help: Checking this option will disable hardware large receive offloading (LRO). This offloading is broken in some hardware drivers, and may impact performance with some specific NICs.

field.label: VLAN Hardware Filtering
field.help: Set usage of VLAN hardware filtering. This hardware acceleration may be broken in a particular device driver, or may impact performance.

field.label: Block private networks
field.help: When set, this option blocks traffic from IP addresses that are reserved for private networks as per RFC 1918 as well as loopback, link-local and Carrier-grade NAT addresses. This option should only be set for WAN interfaces that use the public IP address space.

field.label: Block bogon networks
field.help: When set, this option blocks traffic from IP addresses that are reserved (but not RFC 1918) or not yet assigned by IANA. Bogons are prefixes that should never appear in the Internet routing table, and obviously should not appear as the source address in any packets you receive.

field.label: IPv4 Configuration Type
field.help: The primary type for this interface for IPv4 communication.

field.label: Alias IPv4 address
field.help: The value in this field is used as a fixed alias IPv4 address by the DHCP client.

field.label: Alias IPv4 subnet mask
field.help: The value in this field is used as a fixed alias IPv4 subnet by the DHCP client.

field.label: Reject Leases From
field.help: If there are certain upstream DHCP servers that should be ignored, place the comma separated list of IP addresses of the DHCP servers to be ignored here. This is useful for rejecting leases from cable modems that offer private IPs when they lose upstream sync.

field.label: Hostname
field.help: The value in this field is sent as the DHCP client identifier and hostname when requesting a DHCP lease. Some ISPs may require this (for client identification).

field.label: Honour MTU
field.help: An ISP may incorrectly set an MTU value which can cause intermittent network disruption. By default this value will be ignored. Setting this option will allow to apply the MTU supplied by the ISP instead.

field.label: Use VLAN priority
field.help: Certain ISPs may require that DHCPv4 requests are sent with a specific VLAN priority.

field.label: Send Options
field.help: Options to send to the server, one per line.

field.label: Request Options
field.help: Options to request from the server, one per line.

field.label: IPv6 Configuration Type
field.help: The primary type for this interface for IPv6 communication.

field.label: Use VLAN priority
field.help: Certain ISPs may require that DHCPv6 requests are sent with a specific VLAN priority.

field.label: Prefix delegation size
field.help: The value in this field is the delegated prefix length provided by the DHCPv6 server.

field.label: Request prefix only
field.help: Only request an IPv6 prefix; do not request an IPv6 address.

field.label: Information Only
field.help: Prevent asking for an IPv6 address, only request configuration parameters like DNS etc.

field.label: Request DNS configuration
field.help: Request DNS configuration from the server.

field.label: Send prefix hint
field.help: Send an IPv6 prefix hint to indicate the desired prefix size for delegation

field.label: Send rapid commit
field.help: Send a rapid-commit option in solicit messages and wait for an immediate reply instead of advertisements.

field.label: Optional prefix ID
field.help: The value in this field is the delegated hexadecimal IPv6 prefix ID. This determines the configurable /64 network ID based on the dynamic IPv6 connection.

field.label: Optional interface ID
field.help: The value in this field is the numeric IPv6 interface ID used to construct the lower part of the resulting IPv6 prefix address. Setting a hex value will use that fixed value in its lower address part. Please note the maximum usable value is 0x7fffffffffffffff due to a PHP integer restriction.

field.label: Optional prefix IAID
field.help: The ID to use for prefix request identity association if required to be non-standard.

field.label: Send Options
field.help: Options to send to the server, one per line.

field.label: Request Options
field.help: Options to send to the server, one per line.

field.label: 6RD prefix
field.help: The value in this field is the 6RD IPv6 prefix assigned by your ISP. e.g. '2001:db8::/32'

field.label: 6RD Border Relay
field.help: The value in this field is 6RD IPv4 gateway address assigned by your ISP

field.label: 6RD IPv4 Prefix length
field.help: The value in this field is the 6RD IPv4 prefix length. A value of 0 means we embed the entire IPv4 address in the 6RD prefix.

field.label: 6RD IPv4 Prefix address
field.help: The value in this field is the 6RD IPv4 prefix address. Optionally overrides the automatic detection.

field.label: Parent interface
field.help: This selects the dynamic IPv6 WAN interface to track for configuration.

field.label: Assign prefix ID
field.help: The value in this field is the delegated hexadecimal IPv6 prefix ID. This determines the configurable /64 network ID based on the dynamic IPv6 connection.

field.label: Reserved prefix range
field.help: The value in this field is the length of the reserved prefix range for downstream prefix delegation. The range starts at the given prefix ID. The default is to only reserve the given prefix ID.

field.label: Optional interface ID
field.help: The value in this field is the numeric IPv6 interface ID used to construct the lower part of the resulting IPv6 prefix address. Setting a hex value will use that fixed value in its lower address part. Please note the maximum usable value is 0x7fffffffffffffff due to a PHP integer restriction.

field.label: Optional prefix IAID
field.help: The ID to use for prefix request identity association if required to be non-standard.

field.label: Manual configuration
field.help: If this option is set, you will be able to manually set the DHCPv6 and Router Advertisements service for this interface. Use with care.

field.label: Dynamic gateway policy
field.help: If the destination is directly reachable via an interface requiring no intermediary system to act as a gateway, you can select this option which allows dynamic gateways to be created without direct target addresses. Some tunnel types support this.

field.label: IPv4 gateway rules
field.help: Select a gateway from the list to reply the incoming packets to the proper next hop on their way back and apply source NAT when configured. This is typically disabled for LAN type interfaces.

field.label: IPv6 gateway rules
field.help: Select a gateway from the list to reply the incoming packets to the proper next hop on their way back. This is typically disabled for LAN type interfaces.
